pr_title: Fix changing time during fall daylight savings transition
pr_body:
<!--
About this template

The following template aims to help contributors write a good description for their pull requests.
We'd like you to provide a description of the changes in your pull request (i.e. bugs fixed or features added), motivation behind the changes, and complete the checklist below before opening a pull request.

Feel free to discard it if you need to (e.g. when you just fix a typo). -->

### Motivation / Background

Fixes #45055
<!-- Describe why this Pull Request needs to be merged. What bug have you fixed? What feature have you added? Why is it important? -->

This Pull Request has been created because of an issue changing or advancing time during the autumn daylight savings time time change. The issue relates to how an hour repeats during the fall DST time change (there are two 1ams), but in Time#change we create a new time using just the integer hour. When creating the new time using the hour of 1, we always choose to use the first 1am. This change makes it so if the hour is being changed then the old behavior happens (the first 1am is used) but if the hour isn't being changed, and `self` is using the second 1am, then we use the second 1am.

### Detail

This Pull Request changes Time#change, but also affects Time#advance

### Additional information

<!-- Provide additional information such as benchmarks, reference to other repositories or alternative solutions. -->

pr_comments:
#45556 was previously opened to partially address #45055, and I had left a suggestion there for a more precise solution.  Unfortunately, the author never responded.

I think the problem is more extensive than #45055 indicates, and the solution in this PR may not cover all cases.  Though my suggestion in #45556 didn't either because it only addressed local times.

Building on my suggestion from #45556, I've opened #46251 and included thorough test coverage of local and non-local times, as well as whole- and fractional-hour DST offsets, for both `Time#change` and `Time#advance`.

@khall, I have added you as a co-author.

issue_context.title: Time#advance and Time#change behave incorrectly at fall Daylight Saving Time change
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

Run the following RSpec:

```ruby
require 'active_support/time'

describe Time do
  before { Time.zone = 'Europe/Lisbon' }
  let(:time) { Time.new(2021, 10, 31, 0, 0, 0, Time.zone).advance(hours: 2) }

  context '#advance' do
    it 'works correctly at fall DST change' do
      expect(time.advance(seconds: 0) - time).to eq(0)
    end
  end

  context '#change' do
    it 'works correctly at fall DST change' do
      expect(time.change(sec: 0) - time).to eq(0)
    end
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior

Specs pass.

### Actual behavior

Specs fail as follows:

```
  1) Time#advance works correctly at fall DST change
     Failure/Error: expect(time.advance(seconds: 0) - time).to eq(0)
     
       expected: 0
            got: 3600.0
     
       (compared using ==)
     # ./backend/spec/rails_time_advance_dst_spec.rb:7:in `block in <main>'

  2) Time#change works correctly at fall DST change
     Failure/Error: expect(time.change(sec: 0) - time).to eq(0)
     
       expected: 0
            got: 3600.0
     
       (compared using ==)
     # ./backend/spec/rails_time_advance_dst_spec.rb:13:in `block in <main>'
```

### System configuration

**Rails version**: 6.1.5.1

**Ruby version**: 2.6.8p0 (jruby 9.3.4.0)

### Notes

The bug is probably also reproducible on Rails 7.0.3, since [the relevant code](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v7.0.3//activesupport/lib/active_support/core_ext/time/calculations.rb#L138) hasn't changed [since 6.1.5.1](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v6.1.5.1/activesupport/lib/active_support/core_ext/time/calculations.rb#L139).

Using ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone instead of Time (i.e. replacing `Time.new(..., Time.zone)` with `Time.zone.local(...)`) makes the specs pass, and can be an acceptable workaround. Nonetheless, since ActiveSupport does attempt and claim to support working with Time objects, and provides the `change` and `advance` methods for them, I consider this a bug. FWIW, it has bit me in practice while writing tests for DST handling in our time-related code. 

The specs above are the shortest and simplest examples I've found that clearly display the incorrect behavior. There's probably some need for more comprehensive test coverage for time handling around DST changes in general, as I can think of several possible tweaks to the behavior that could probably make the specs above pass while still leaving the underlying bug(s) unfixed.

In particular, note that the `time` fixture set up for the specs above is arguably already a somewhat broken object: it stringifies to "2021-10-31 02:00:00 +0100", which is not a time that exists in the Lisbon time zone, as the clock should've jumped back to 01:00:00 +0000 at that moment. My original code, of which the above is a condensed version, stepped the time forward by one minute increments using `advance(minutes: 1)`; the `time` value above is where things broke down when doing that.
comments:
change method needs to use sec instead of seconds.

```
irb(main):001:0> time = Time.new(2000, 01, 01)
=> 2000-01-01 00:00:00 -0200
irb(main):002:0> time.change(seconds: 10)
=> 2000-01-01 00:00:00 -0200
irb(main):003:0> time.change(sec: 10)
=> 2000-01-01 00:00:10 -0200
```

@kaiquekandykoga Thanks. I've fixed the spec above. It doesn't actually change the failure in any way, though. Indeed, even passing an empty hash (i.e. `time.change({})`) will trigger the same misbehavior.

[Executable test case](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#create-an-executable-test-case):

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

  gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
end

require "active_support"
require "active_support/time"
require "minitest/autorun"

Time.zone = 'Europe/Lisbon'

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_advance
    time = Time.new(2021, 10, 31, 0, 0, 0, Time.zone).advance(hours: 2)
    assert_equal 0, time.advance(seconds: 0) - time
  end

  def test_change
    time = Time.new(2021, 10, 31, 0, 0, 0, Time.zone).advance(hours: 2)
    assert_equal 0, time.change(seconds: 0) - time
  end
end
```

review_comments:
This check is expensive. Since UTC times are very common and not concerned, it would be best to avoid this computation in such case.

I'd also not use ternaries here, as it really doesn't help readability.
